common: Purely instrumental: no vocals, no singing, no humming, no spoken words, no voices, no crowd or audience noise. Background score for a lively, witty YouTube explainer: steady groove and consistent energy and volume from the first second to the last, no slow intro, no breakdowns, no fade-out until the final seconds. Bright, clean professional mix.

beds.noir: playful 1960s caper-movie detective jazz at 118 BPM: walking upright bass, crisp swinging brushed drums, finger snaps, vibraphone and muted trumpet riffs, cheeky and curious, major key
beds.lounge: upbeat 1960s Las Vegas swing at 126 BPM: bright big-band brass stabs, swinging drums, upright bass, vibraphone, glamorous, fun and confident, major key
beds.slots: bouncy hypnotic casino-arcade groove at 120 BPM: twinkling glockenspiel and vibraphone arpeggios, funky bass, tight drums, playful and slightly mischievous, major key
beds.tension: driving heist-movie tension at 128 BPM: staccato strings, pulsing bass, crisp snare, bongos, suspenseful but exciting like a casino-robbery montage, energetic, not sad
beds.curious: quirky upbeat explainer music at 112 BPM: pizzicato strings, marimba, clarinet, light claps and finger snaps, curious and witty, major key
beds.serious: cinematic building reveal at 100 BPM: steady pulsing piano eighth notes, rising strings, light driving percussion, intriguing and confident, builds anticipation, hopeful, not sad
beds.finale: triumphant upbeat 1960s big-band swing finale at 132 BPM: full brass section, swinging drums, joyful and satisfying, major key

stings.fanfare: a short triumphant brass fanfare with a cymbal crash, like a 1950s game-show win, then silence
stings.reveal: a short dramatic orchestral 'dun-dun' brass and timpani sting for a revelation, then silence
stings.closed: a short brass chord with a big timpani hit, like a rubber stamp slamming a case closed in a 1950s detective film, then silence
stings.jackpot: a short twinkling slot-machine jackpot jingle with bells, then silence
